text: When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land he is giving you, and you drive them out and settle in their cities and their houses,
you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
Build roads to them, and divide into three regions the territory that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills another may flee there.
This is the rule for the one who kills another and flees there to save his life: anyone who strikes down his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in the past.

versions.text: This is the case of the killer who may flee there and live: anyone who strikes down his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in the past.
versions.explanation: 'The case of the killer' is legally stiff and reads awkwardly aloud; דְּבַר here means the rule or provision governing such a person, and וָחָי conveys the purpose of preserving his life. The revised wording is clearer and flows better in oral reading.

text: Suppose a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and as his hand swings the axe to fell a tree, the head slips off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies. Such a man may flee to one of these cities and live.

Otherwise the avenger of blood might pursue the killer in the heat of his anger, overtake him because the way is long, and take his life—though he did not deserve to die, since he had not hated his neighbor in the past.
That is why I command you: set apart three cities for yourself.
And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land he promised to give them—
if you carefully keep all this commandment that I give you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways always—then you shall add three more cities to these three,

versions.text: because you carefully keep all this commandment that I give you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways always—then you shall add three more cities to these three,
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כִּי here introduces a condition parallel to the conditional clause of verse 8 ('And if the LORD your God enlarges…'), with the apodosis being 'then you shall add three more cities.' Rendering it 'because' turns a condition into a statement of fact and obscures the conditional structure; 'if' preserves both the syntax and the rhythm of the sentence.

text: so that innocent blood is not shed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt does not come upon you.
But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, attacks him and takes his life, and then flees to one of these cities,
the elders of his own city shall send for him and bring him back from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die.
Show him no pity. Purge from Israel the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and it will go well with you.
Do not move your neighbor's boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you receive in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
A single witness is not enough to convict anyone of any crime or offense he may have committed. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If a malicious witness comes forward against someone, accusing him of wrongdoing,
the two parties to the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office at that time.
The judges shall investigate the matter thoroughly, and if the witness proves to be a liar, giving false testimony against his brother,
then do to him what he intended to do to his brother. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
The rest will hear of it and be afraid, and never again will such an evil thing be done among you.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
